title: What If the Amazon Rainforest Vanished?

scenes.text: What if the Amazon vanished? Everyone fears for our air. That is not the real danger.
First, carbon: the forest holds more than one hundred billion tonnes, and losing it would release much into the air.
Within years, less rain. The Amazon makes about half its own rainfall, so dry seasons would lengthen and droughts spread.
Scientists warn of a tipping point at roughly twenty to twenty five percent lost, past which forest could become dry savanna.
Gone too: at least one tenth of all known species, living on about one percent of Earth's surface.
Yet our oxygen would barely change. Experts say its net oxygen output is about zero. We would lose climate, not breath.

description:
What if the Amazon rainforest vanished?
Carbon released, rainfall cut, a possible tipping point near 20 to 25 percent lost, and a tenth of known species gone. But not our oxygen.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which place on Earth would you save first? What should we run through next?
